subject: Using hk permutations thresholds for scantwo (binary model, selective gt'ing -> used EM)

messages.author: 98a3d43f8b16bc07
messages.subject: Using hk permutations thresholds for scantwo (binary model, selective gt'ing -> used EM)
parts:
Hello,
I have selective genotyping of an F2 for both case/control individuals (binary pheno). For this design, the EM method for QTL scanning is recommended rather than Haley-Knott (as per Manichaikul 2009) However, even low iteration scantwo permutations take extremely long with EM/Binary. Will the use of the faster Haley-Knott method for permutation upwardly skew LOD thresholds? The initial scantwo was performed with EM/Binary.  

On a side note- I have a relatively low number of individuals (low resolution), so LOD is elevated for a large portion of one or two chromosomes. Permutation on those chromosomes leads to high global thresholds. Is it appropriate to drop my two major effect QTL chromosomes for permutations for scanning for other possible minor effect QTL?

Thanks!!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Using hk permutations thresholds for scantwo (binary model, selective gt'ing -> used EM)
parts:
You want the methods used in the permutations to match that used in the analysis.

Are you seeking epistatic interactions, despite the binary trait, selective genotyping, and low number of individuals? If you just focus on main effect QTL, you can skip the two-dimensional scan.

I don't quite understand your second paragraph.

karl
